description: [MÉDIA] 5 — Collaborator routes have no declarative guard; each handler manually calls requireAuth/requirePasswordChanged, so a new endpoint is public by omission. Migrate to class-level NestJS guards following the main auth module pattern, PRESERVING the FEAT-003 tokenVersion revocation check. This feature carries test-rewrite risk (the existing colaborador-revocation.spec.ts tests the controller directly) and is sequenced last. Independent of FEAT-001/002/003 at the file level.
steps: Create src/colaborador/colaborador-public.decorator.ts: `export const COLABORADOR_PUBLIC_KEY = 'colaborador_public'; export const ColaboradorPublic = () => SetMetadata(COLABORADOR_PUBLIC_KEY, true);` (mirror src/auth/roles.decorator.ts).

Create src/colaborador/colaborador.decorator.ts: a `@Colaborador()` param decorator via createParamDecorator returning `request.colaborador` (mirror src/auth/current-user.decorator.ts). Type it as ColaboradorTokenPayload from colaborador-session.service.ts.

Create src/colaborador/colaborador-auth.guard.ts: `ColaboradorAuthGuard implements CanActivate`. If Reflector.getAllAndOverride(COLABORADOR_PUBLIC_KEY, [getHandler(), getClass()]) is true, return true (skip). Else extract payload via ColaboradorSessionService.extractFromRequest(req); if null throw UnauthorizedException('Não autorizado.'). Then call ColaboradorService.getRevocationState(payload.funcionarioId) and throw UnauthorizedException when revocation is null OR !revocation.ativo OR revocation.tokenVersion !== payload.tokenVersion (PRESERVE this exact FEAT-003 logic). On success set request.colaborador = payload and return true. Inject ColaboradorSessionService, ColaboradorService, Reflector.

Create src/colaborador/colaborador-require-password-changed.guard.ts: `ColaboradorRequirePasswordChangedGuard implements CanActivate` that reads request.colaborador and throws UnauthorizedException('É necessário alterar a senha antes de acessar o sistema.') when payload.primeiroAcesso is true; passes otherwise. Must run AFTER ColaboradorAuthGuard (mirror RequirePasswordChangedGuard).

In src/colaborador/colaborador.controller.ts: add @UseGuards(ColaboradorAuthGuard, ColaboradorRequirePasswordChangedGuard) at the @Controller('colaborador') class level. Mark auth/login, auth/logout, auth/session with @ColaboradorPublic(). IMPORTANT: getLogo and getSession must NOT be blocked by the password-changed requirement (preserve current behavior — finding [BAIXA] 12 is OUT OF SCOPE). Since the class-level password-changed guard would otherwise block getLogo, handle this: either (a) do NOT put the password-changed guard at class level — instead apply @UseGuards(ColaboradorRequirePasswordChangedGuard) only on the handlers that block today (perfil, listRecibos, getRecibo, getReciboPdf, trocarSenha must NOT require password-changed since it IS the change endpoint), OR (b) add a @ColaboradorPasswordChangeOptional() style metadata the password guard honors. Prefer approach (a): class-level ColaboradorAuthGuard only, plus per-handler @UseGuards(ColaboradorRequirePasswordChangedGuard) on perfil/recibos endpoints. login/logout/session stay @ColaboradorPublic(); logo and trocarSenha get auth (class guard) but NOT password-changed.

Replace each `const payload = await this.requireAuth(req)` with the `@Colaborador() payload: ColaboradorTokenPayload` param (or read request.colaborador). Remove the now-redundant `this.requirePasswordChanged(payload)` calls (the guard covers them). For logout/getSession keep using ColaboradorSessionService.extractFromRequest directly as today (they are public and tolerate missing/invalid tokens) — do not force the guard to 401 them.
Remove the private requireAuth and requirePasswordChanged methods from the controller once all handlers are migrated.

Register the new guards as providers in src/colaborador/colaborador.module.ts (ColaboradorAuthGuard, ColaboradorRequirePasswordChangedGuard). ColaboradorService and ColaboradorSessionService are already providers; Reflector is available from @nestjs/core without registration.

Rewrite src/colaborador/colaborador-revocation.spec.ts: it currently constructs ColaboradorController with 5 args and calls controller.getPerfil(req) to assert revocation. After migration the controller no longer enforces auth. Rewrite the spec to exercise ColaboradorAuthGuard.canActivate directly with a mocked ExecutionContext + Reflector + ColaboradorSessionService + ColaboradorService, covering the same scenarios: version mismatch -> throws, inactive -> throws, missing employee (getRevocationState null) -> throws, happy path -> true and request.colaborador set, @ColaboradorPublic() route -> true without auth. Keep the FEAT-003 description intent in the spec comments.
acceptance_criteria: @Controller('colaborador') enforces authentication declaratively; adding a new handler without extra code is protected by default (not public by omission).
login, logout, session remain publicly reachable; the tokenVersion revocation check still rejects revoked/inactive/mismatched tokens (FEAT-003 preserved).
perfil and all recibos endpoints still require a changed password; logo and trocarSenha remain reachable without the password-changed requirement (behavior preserved).
The rewritten colaborador-revocation.spec.ts passes and tests the guard, not the controller.
verification: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit — no new errors outside the baseline fiscal spec files.
pnpm test src/colaborador — all collaborator specs pass (including the rewritten guard spec).
findings:
Confirmed in base: ColaboradorService.getRevocationState returns { ativo, tokenVersion } | null; controller.requireAuth is async and checks null/!ativo/tokenVersion-mismatch (FEAT-003). Today getLogo and getSession use extractFromRequest WITHOUT requirePasswordChanged (BAIXA 12, out of scope — must stay that way). trocarSenha uses requireAuth but not requirePasswordChanged (it is the change endpoint). The module already provides ColaboradorService + ColaboradorSessionService.

IMPLEMENTED (approach a from steps): Created colaborador-public.decorator.ts (COLABORADOR_PUBLIC_KEY + @ColaboradorPublic), colaborador.decorator.ts (@Colaborador param decorator -> request.colaborador typed as ColaboradorTokenPayload), colaborador-auth.guard.ts (ColaboradorAuthGuard: skips @ColaboradorPublic via Reflector.getAllAndOverride; extractFromRequest null -> 401; getRevocationState null/!ativo/tokenVersion-mismatch -> 401 PRESERVING FEAT-003; on success sets request.colaborador), colaborador-require-password-changed.guard.ts (throws when request.colaborador.primeiroAcesso). Controller: class-level @UseGuards(ColaboradorAuthGuard) only; login/logout/session marked @ColaboradorPublic(); per-handler @UseGuards(ColaboradorRequirePasswordChangedGuard) on perfil, recibos (list/:id/:id/pdf) ONLY; logo + trocarSenha get class auth guard but NOT password-changed (behavior preserved). Replaced requireAuth calls with @Colaborador() param on logo/trocarSenha/perfil/recibos; logout/getSession keep extractFromRequest directly (public, tolerate missing/invalid tokens). Removed private requireAuth/requirePasswordChanged helpers. Registered both guards as providers in colaborador.module.ts. Rewrote colaborador-revocation.spec.ts to exercise ColaboradorAuthGuard.canActivate with mocked ExecutionContext/Reflector/ColaboradorSessionService/ColaboradorService: version-mismatch/inactive/missing-employee/no-token -> throws, happy path -> true + request.colaborador set, @ColaboradorPublic() -> true without touching extractFromRequest.

VERIFICATION: pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -> only the 23 baseline TS2554 errors in fiscal-apuracao.controller.spec.ts + fiscal-entregas.service.spec.ts, NO new errors. pnpm test src/colaborador -> 6/6 pass. pnpm build -> succeeds.
